text:
maria: quick wrap from the 2-day mini GPTQ bake (Llama / Mistral / Qwen). tried the lightweight per-layer reorder + blockwise 8-bit, and a conservative per-channel version. results below, TL;DR at top.

maria: TL;DR: GPTQ gives decent accuracy retention for Qwen, Mistral loses ~2-3 points on MMLU w/ default libs, Llama-2 shows smaller deltas but needs per-channel scales for stable kv caching. Recommend AWQ for Mistral when latency matters; GPTQ for Qwen; Llama->INT8 only with per-channel and extra KV patch.

aj: can you drop the short perf/accuracy table?

maria: sure — small table from eval-run-2026-03-18 (FP32 vs GPTQ8). numbers are median across 3 seeds.

```
Model         | Suite  | FP32  | GPTQ8  | delta
Mistral-7B    | MMLU   | 62.1  | 59.4   | -2.7
Llama-2-7B    | MMLU   | 60.8  | 58.9   | -1.9
Qwen-7B       | MMLU   | 61.5  | 60.7   | -0.8
Mistral-7B    | Hella  | 78.2  | 76.1   | -2.1
Llama-2-7B    | Hella  | 77.0  | 75.6   | -1.4
Qwen-7B       | Hella  | 77.5  | 77.0   | -0.5
```

maria: perf notes: baseline FP32 token/s on our p4d-ish nodes: Mistral ~210 tok/s, Llama ~195 tok/s, Qwen ~220 tok/s. GPTQ8 increased throughput ~1.6-1.9x depending on kernel path. KV cache overhead observed on Llama ~6-8% slower if not using patched aten kernels.

kevin: interesting — did you try AWQ vs GPTQ on Mistral? I recall AWQ helps reduce the delta for many Mistral checkpoints.

maria: yes — quick AWQ pass on Mistral-7B (block size=128) gave MMLU 60.2 (delta -1.9) and similar perf to GPTQ8. AWQ produced slightly noisier tail-case failure on multi-hop QA but better avg.

sophia: any regressions flagged by our quality monitors? specific prompts that break?

maria: flagged 4 prompts from our internal rms-eval promptset: mostly long-context math hallucinations and a few instruction-following edge cases. Attached a small snippet: 

```
Prompt: "Given these constraints, prove or disprove..."
FP32: concise reasoning
GPTQ8 (Mistral): truncated step and incorrect final numeric
```

maria: mitigation ideas — for Llama: enable per-channel quant + kv-cache kernel patch; for Mistral: prefer AWQ with block=128 for canary; for Qwen: GPTQ8 seems safe as default for now.

aj: ops question — how do these map to deployment profiles? like dedicated vs hosted.

maria: quick mapping: hosted (fastest onboarding) -> default to GPTQ8 for Qwen + canary; Dedicated -> customer can choose AWQ for Mistral or conservative INT8 per-channel for Llama; Private/on-prem -> we ship both kernels and a short checklist (KV patch, quant scales, fallback to FP16) for safe rollout.

ops-bot: note saved to /runs/gptq-mini-20260318/metadata.json and created canary config: canary/gptq-mistral-awq-128.json

kevin: thanks — can you add short instructions for the canary? I can run infra for the canary tomorrow.

maria: will add a 5-step canary in the thread: 1) build quant artifact (hash ab12f3), 2) deploy to canary pool (2 nodes), 3) enable tracing for those routes, 4) run 10k prompt sweep (rms-eval), 5) rollback threshold delta <=1.5 points MMLU or error rate increase <=0.5%.

sophia: +1 on rollback thresholds. Also let's tag product for any customer-impacting changes. @aj can you ping them?

aj: will do. pinged @product in #product-private.

maria: notes for followups: produce a condensed bake slide (1 pager), push AWQ/GPTQ kernel diffs into repo, and schedule a longer sweep including AWQ params (bs=64/128/256) next week.

eval-bot: eval summary artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/gptq-mini-20260318/summary.json

maria: thanks everyone, I'll drop the 1-pager and canary checklist by EOD.
